Demolition - When this mutant destroys a building, add 2/2/3/3/5 random Parts to your hand.

Before this mutant didn’t have any stats, it now has a Parts generation ability and its high stats allow it to destroy buildings easily.

Raptoid - Zoo/Tech
ATK 3/5/6/8/11
HP 2/3/4/6/8

Autorepair 1/1/2/2/3
Passive - Whenever this mutant is targeted by a Parts card, it gains 1 EVO. (Platinum: Whenever one of your mutants is targeted by a Parts card, it gains 1 EVO).

Before, this mutant only had Autorepair. We chose to give it an Adaptation ability tied to Parts, giving it more flexibility in the possible archetypes it can be played in.

R0B-H4N Sentinel - Tech
ATK 3/6/8/11/13
HP 3/5/6/9/11

Autorepair 1/1/2/2/3
Passive - At the start of the Autorepair phase, if this mutant is undamaged, it gains +1/1/2/2/3 HP. 

This mutant only had the Armor and Autorepair keywords. It no longer has Armor but can increase its maximum HP as long as it’s kept at full health.

Horus - Mystic/Zoo
ATK 1/2/3/4/6
HP 4/6/7/9/12

Action : Inflicts Burning1/1/2/3/4 to each opposing mutant. 

We decided to modify Horus' ability. Instead of inflicting Burning through Ignite and a Passive at the end of the turn, we decided to give it the ability to do so through an Action Ability. It reinforces its Mystic theme and allows more control to the player.

Building Cards

Junkyard Crane
5 HP
2 EVO

Passive - Whenever one of your Tech mutants is destroyed, create a random Parts card in your hand.

The old version of this card had a too complicated trigger (to have a Part in hand at the start of the turn). We decided to keep the idea to get Parts back but associated with the thematic of mutant destruction.

Recycling Tower
5 HP
2 EVO

Passive - Whenever an Ephemeral card is erased from your hand, heal 1 from your Psycore.

The old version of Recycling Tower often had the same use as the Repair Nanite Parts card. We decided to remove the Part Card Reinforced Structure allowing the Psycore to be healed while adding its effect to this new version of the Recycling Tower.

World-Tree
5 HP
2 EVO

Passive - At the beginning of your turn, heal 1 to your Psycore and draw a card. 
We felt that the card was largely lacking in power. So we decided to replace its ability to self-maintain with a draw effect. 

Support Cards

Orbs

Repair Orb
The equipped mutant has +1 HP and Autorepair 2.

This highly defensive orb replaces the old version of the Repair Orb. The power of the card has been greatly increased.

Fury Orb
The equipped mutant has +3 ATK and you immediately deal 2 damage to it. 
This risky offensive orb replaces the old version of the Fury Orb. The old version was an obsolete design. 

Invasion Orb
The equipped mutant has +1 ATK and +1 HP for each non-Psycore building on your opponent's battlefield.
This orb is consistent with the new version of the Alien. The old version was an obsolete design. 

Vampiric Orb (replaces Sacrifice orb)
When the equipped mutant damages another mutant, it heals 2 from itself.

This orb replaces the Sacrificial Orb. The former version was a mash-up of test-mechanics moved to other cards during development (Protector Orb and Power Orb).

Blazing Orb (replaces Ignite)
Whenever the mutant equipped with this orb deals damage to another mutant, il also inflicts Burning 1. 

This orb replaces the Ignite Orb. Instead of limiting the orb to triggering on attacks, it works on all damage dealt (including with abilities).

Gadgets

Nano-bomb
Deals 1 damage to any target. 

This Gadget card replaces the Gadget - Reinforced Structure card. The previous one didn't work as well as expected, and in order not to change the number of gadgets available, we have chosen to introduce a gadget capable of inflicting direct damage. The damage is limited, however, so as not to make it an overpowered card. 

Other Support cards

Psycore Overload
Your Psycore takes 3 damage. Summon a Basic copy of your Starter mutant.
The card was too powerful in its previous version. So we made the choice to change from a card dedicated to the draw to a card allowing to play more mutants.

Second Chance
Discard a Necro Mutant. Summon a Zombie. 

The previous version allowing to recover a mutant from the discard pile did not work as expected. So we chose to reinforce the swarming aspect of the Necro. 

Remelt Steel
Add an Orb card fro your discard pile to your hand. 
We have removed the cost of discarding the card, to make it more interesting. 

Spoils of War
Discard a Blades Mutant. Add an orb deck from your deck to your hand. 

We removed the randomness, by adding a discard cost. This makes the card more reliable in a deck with many different orb cards.

Rebalanced Cards
Cards with more minor changes, often only numerical. 

Mutant Cards

Honey Bunny -Basic - Blades/Zoo
ATK 2/3/5/6/9
HP 1/2/4/5/8

Evasion
Tactics - while you have another mutant without Evasion, this mutant has +1/2/3/4/5 ATK
Honey Bunny is now more fragile (while still taking advantage of her Evasion).

The Devourer - Advanced - Necro/Space
ATK 3/5/7/10/13
HP 3/5/7/10/13

Passive - Once per turn, when a Bones would be added to your discard pile, instead it is erased and this mutant gains +1/1/1/1/2 ATK and +1/1/1/1/2 HP until the end of turn. 
This mutant took advantage far too easily of effects that put several bones in the discard pile, even at the lowest ranks.

Retribution - Basic - Mystic
ATK 1/2/3/4/5
HP 2/3/5/7/9

Action: Heals 2/3/4/5/8 to target allied mutant and Cleanse all the Status Conditions of the target. 
This mutant was too passive, so we decided to increase its ATK at the expense of its HP. We've also increased its active ability, both in magnitude and by adding the Cleanse effect to all ranks (instead of keeping it only on high ranks).

Cyber-Agent - Advanced - Blades/Tech
ATK 2/3/4/6/9
HP 2/4/6/8/11

Autorepair 1/1/1/1/2
Tactics - While this mutant is undamaged, this mutant has +2/3/4/5/6 ATK. 
The mutant has been adjusted to give more value to its Tactics, while giving it Autorepair from the Basic rank. 

Support Cards

Darwinism
Target Mutant gains 2 EVO. 

The card gives 2 EVO instead of 3, because it was too powerful compared to the power level we wanted for this card.

Small Medpack
Heals 1 damage from target damaged allied mutant, then draw 1 card. 

The card was used more for its draw effect than for its healing effect. In order to rebalance this, it now requires a wounded mutant to be healed in order to work, and can no longer be played on an intact mutant.

notes.title: Early access feature #1 : the art of crafting
notes.content:
Among the new features available at the early access launch of Mutants: Genesis, today we're having a close up on the deckbuilding menu, specifically the crafting tool, the must-have for tweaking your decks and gaining power. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/df41c304fa1b42515c359768a93df5069f921e6c.png

Currency
In Mutants: Genesis, it is possible for players to create specific cards from a dedicated currency called Mutagens.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/0d7ed6c6557f3f1608f4bf440f569fed1f1b5053.png Mutagens logo

This currency is obtained by recycling extra copies of cards obtained through capsules. The player can see how many Mutagens they currently have at the top of the screen.

Recycling
When a player opens a capsule, if they get a card that they already have the maximum number of copies of (1 for heroic cards, 3 for all others), then the card is automatically recycled.

In exchange, the player gets a fixed number of Mutagens, depending on the rarity of the card.

Unowned cards
From the deckbuilding menu, players can use their Mutagens to create cards of their choice.

The Crafting tool is integrated into the deckbuilding menu: now players can access the unowned cards in their collection. 

These cards will appear when the Unowned option at the top of the screen is activated. Unowned cards will appear in the collection in a grayed out format. An unowned card can be found in a decklist, if it comes from a deck import. The boxes are also grayed out.

⚠️ If a player does not have enough copies of a card in a list, the owned and unowned copies are split into two boxes: one solid, one grayed out, each with its own copy counter.

When a player interacts with an unowned card (left-click to put it in the deck from the collection, or right-click from anywhere to open the detailed info), the detailed info pops up directly in craft mode.

Campaign cards are not craftable. ⚠️

Copy dots
The possession indicator under the cards has been changed.

From now on, there should always be a dot for each maximum possible copy of a card. Heroic cards will always have 1 dot, all others will have 3 dots. These dots have three states: not owned, owned and not present in the deck, and owned in the deck. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/0e8194f6e9ffea562bb6d3795f7f88b75c217c2e.png Unowned
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/0a71d853e72e4483e0ec0c0497e3781425e0ba1f.png Owned but not in the deck
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/732cd6f4972d78fd2d94ecd3187bebd6acb3bf29.png Owned in the deck

Craft Mode

In the deckbuilding screen only, the detailed info popup of a card is enhanced.
When a player tries to put a copy of an unowned card into their deck, instead of nothing happening, the game will open the detailed info popup of the card in question, directly opened in Craft mode.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/77891cca87f73f7f3005f6cd038d19e5e0bc470e.png

In this mode, the player will be able to create a new copy of the card in exchange for his Mutagens.

Here is the information about this special mode in the popup:


 A reminder of the mutagens owned
 A reminder of the owned card copies
 An information button: when clicked, a popup containing text appears indicating how the crafting system works.

 The Craft button: with an upper part depending on the rarity (See below: Special cases: Ultra and Heroic Craft) and several possible situations: 
 the player has enough Mutagens
 the player does not have enough Mutagens
 the player now has the maximum number of copies
 the card is not craftable

 The mode switching button: by clicking on this button, the player goes back to detailed information mode. He can switch back to craft mode via the same button, also located in detailed information mode.

Special Cases: Ultra and Heroic Cards
There is an additional limitation regarding Ultra and Heroic cards crafting.
These cards, in addition to requiring Mutagens, require a special item called the Ultra/Heroic Energy Core.

Players can have a maximum of 3 Ultra Energy Cores and 1 Heroic Energy Core.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/b1f49d53c5f854ff031aa8c3c9525e01393a76ae.png Ultra
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/8dbcba7001bc4849176aa51f6794ba322e9a3e83.png Heroic

If a player does not have a Core when attempting to craft Ultra or Heroic, the button is locked. Players will be able to obtain Energy Cores through weekly quests, the Battle Pass, or as event rewards.

Capsule Information
If a player needs to obtain a Core via any means and already has the maximum number, a popup will offer to turn their Core into Mutagens.

Deck Invalidity
With the appearance of the crafting system, and the possibility of importing a deck without having all the cards, decks must now have a status of validity or invalidity.

It is possible to have invalid decks in your deck collection, but it is not possible to select them to play with as long as their status is invalid.

An Invalid deck is surrounded by a red effect. A popup window indicates "This deck is invalid, because it is not complete, or contains unowned or temporarily disabled cards".

A deck is invalid if it meets one of these conditions: 


 The deck does not contain 40 cards
 The deck contains at least one unowned card
 The deck contains at least one deactivated card


It is still possible to save an invalid deck. A confirmation popup should ask the player if he/she is sure he/she wants to save this deck despite its status.

In the deck selection screens before deckbuilding, invalid decks appear with the same effect and invalidity icon:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/2570dce0e5828eff13b7f14336dd2ee651f831d6.png

In the deck selection screen before a fight, the deck is additionally grayed out and not interactive: 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/b5eb2e9be58d35d71b6440ac5a0edc2671f4295c.png

And that's it! You know everything about the crafting tool. As a reminder, it will be available at the early access launch of Mutants: Genesis! Don't hesitate to give us your feedback in comments, we are very curious to have your opinion on this feature. Join us also on Discord to exchange between players, share your decklists and debate about the title of best mutant! 

See you soon on Mutants: Genesis 💪

notes.title: What is Mutants: Genesis?
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

With our game announcement, it is clear we wanted ot give you a bit of details on what is the game and how it is played, so here we go!

So what is Mutants: Genesis?

Mutants: Genesis is a free-to-play online card game that makes players take the role of Psycogs, powerful humans with the ability to control mutants.

In Mutants: Genesis your objective will be to prevail on the battlefield by destroying your opponent’s Psycore while defending your own in PvP or defeating the various enemies that will challenge you in PvE.

To do that, you will use a deck of 40 cards that will use a combination of different abilities to ensure your dominance.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/fdc6d340323d289fad69322bd0e1fed65edf43fc.jpg

Mutants: Genesis and its cards

Mutants: Genesis is a turn by turn card game. You and your opponent will each take turns to play cards in the best way possible to take the advantage.

First, you’ll have to build a deck by choosing a Gene that will define your Psycore, this will also limit which cards you can put in your deck and your Starting Card. The Starting Card is a basic Mutant that will be available to you each turn.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/c16eae135318f9d0df9b9d6bc365ed550c0f15e3.jpg

Cards come in different types. You have your Mutants, which are your main tools and can be divided in 3 categories : basic, advanced and heroic. 

 You can play up to 1 basic card each turn directly on the battlefield.
 Advanced are generally stronger and will require that you incubate them first for 1 to 2 turns.
 Heroics have a huge impact on the game but need more time to incubate.

You can have up to 5 Mutants on the field.

Incubation is one of the key differences with other card games. Mutants: Genesis does not have ressources like : mana, lands, etc. Instead, you will need to incubate some Mutants cards by putting them in your Psycore or buildings that allow you to do that. They will then stay there for a set number of turns indicated on the card.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/ef86b590645b9e7d975763ae8989ad848e7b31c7.jpg

Other cards you can find are: support and buildings. 

 Support cards will trigger an effect when played and then be discarded.
 Buildings will take one of the 3 slots available on your board and provide different bonuses or abilities while they are in play : some may allow you to incubate more, draw or trigger specific abilities when you do something in particular.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/ec2ab9e7290b4602077487391580be44e3041d55.jpg

Now here is a quick look about what informations you can find on the Mutant Cards:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/4c417055cab704fa75073d8fc1418d9eb083563e.png

Once you have made your deck using those 3 types of cards you are ready to face the challenges of Mutants: Genesis!

How is Mutants: Genesis played?

Each player starts with a hand of card, the first player will have 5 and the second 6. You can mulligan, meaning putting back in the deck any number of cards you deem unnecessary in your opening hand and then drawing new ones.

Once this is done, it is your turn: it is now time to try to destroy the opponent’s Psycore!

To do that, you can play:

 Up to one basic mutant and incubate as many mutants as you can - your psycore can incubate up to one mutant if none is currently being incubated. 
 As many buildings as you have available slots - up to 3.
 As many support cards as you want. 

But keep in mind the principle of card advantage! Card advantage is totalling the amount of cards on the board and in your hand, the higher the better : it means you have possibilities of play.

Each turn starts, you’ll draw a card and get your Starting Basic Mutant. Your Mutants can attack directly when they are summoned (Except during the first round of the game!). They can target any mutants or building on the board, except when some abilities like Guardian come into play.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/e079a020e21ff6cb84925c6107b4b6f8cb0a9676.jpg

All there is left to do is to win the game!

You now know how to play Mutants: Genesis. Don’t worry, when you will get your hands on the game you’ll have the opportunity to go through a Tutorial to learn some more tips and tricks.

Have a great day Students!
